titulo: Vault, owner, and approval through Telegram
lead: Telegram is optional. @BotFather is Telegram’s official account for creating bots; the token is your bot’s secret code, and the ID is your account number. The token stays in the vault; only registered IDs can talk to the bot. The project tests used a local fake server.
objetivo: Prepare the token in the vault and set the owner ID so the bot only responds to the authorized person.

aprende.t: Keep the token outside the config
Find and register the owner ID
Understand /sim and /nao without promising a live test

hero_alt: Editorial photograph representing the vault, owner, and approval through Telegram.

secoes.sub: Without a registered owner, the bot only responds to /id.

nos.detalhe: On Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, choose a name and username, and copy the token (the bot’s secret code). Save it with the cofre guardar telegram command; don’t paste it into a project file.
Send /id to your bot. It replies, “Your ID is [number]. Put it in telegram_donos in config.json.” The configurar command fills in that same field without editing the JSON by hand.
A message from another ID is ignored and recorded in the audit.
When a command requires a decision, the bot asks and waits for the person who made the request to respond.

secoes.legenda: Click each part to see what it does.

secoes.titulo: Turn this on only if you plan to use it
secoes.sub: Click each step to see what to do.

texto: Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot, choose a name, then choose a username that ends in bot. Copy the token you receive: it’s the bot’s secret code. Don’t paste it into USER.md, AGENTS.md, or config.json. @BotFather also sends your bot’s link in the format t.me/bot_name: open that link to chat with it.
The guardar telegram command asks for the token without displaying it. The configuration file stores the IDs, not the token.

Turn on the bot, send /id, and write down the number. The actual message says “Put it in telegram_donos in config.json.” You can fill in that same field using configurar, when asked for Telegram IDs. Stop the bot with Ctrl+C before configuring it.

Enter the ID when asked for owners, then turn the bot on again. Test with another account if you have one; only yours should get a reply. If a command asks for approval, reply /sim or /nao within 120 seconds; after that, the request expires and the command won’t run.

secoes.sub: Copy the commands and run them in the terminal from the specified folder.

blocos.rot: Terminal · store the token and find your ID
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/intelecto-v2
python3 -m intelecto cofre guardar telegram
python3 -m intelecto telegram

blocos.rot: Terminal · register the owner and turn it on
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/intelecto-v2
python3 -m intelecto configurar
python3 -m intelecto verificar
python3 -m intelecto telegram

abas.html: Automated tests use a fake Telegram server: owner filtering, message format, and approval with /sim. INEMA has not tested the bot live.

secoes.sub: Optional. It depends on your bot and account; INEMA has not tested this integration live.

exercicios.texto: If you use Telegram, get your /id, enter the number in configurar, and turn the bot on again. If you don’t use it, skip this step; it won’t block the rest of the course.
exercicios.pronto: The bot replies to your ID; another account won’t get a reply, if you can test with one.

exercicios.texto: In your bot’s chat, send “rode: echo teste > nota.txt”. This asks for approval because it writes a file. Reply /nao first; use /sim only if you really want to create the file. Approval expires after 120 seconds without /sim or /nao.
exercicios.pronto: The audit records the decision, and the command doesn’t run after /nao.

secoes.sub: Choose before opening the explanation. If you get it wrong, use the link to review.

perguntas.p: Where should you store the bot token?
perguntas.explica: The vault stores the encrypted secret. telegram_donos contains user IDs only.

perguntas.p: What does the bot do when no owner is registered?
opcoes: Replies to anyone who has the link
perguntas.explica: The code keeps /id available so you can find the number and ignores other messages.

perguntas.p: What evidence for Telegram is available in the sources?
opcoes: Several months of continuous public use
Tests with a local fake server
perguntas.explica: The integration was tested against a fake server, not live. Students need to verify it with their own bot.

itens.texto: The token stays in the vault; the ID stays in the configuration.
The automated test does not prove live operation on Telegram.
